numbered_sources.title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 3: - Coming off a Tuesday jog through, the Niners had their longest and perhaps most daunting practice yet Wednesday. It's by design. They have a new practice regiment they're trying out in this year's camp. They will do two days of practice, a jog through, a "high" (long) practice and then a day off. The plan is to then repeat that cycle as camp goes a long. If the hope was to help reduce injuries, the early returns aren't promising but there's a long way to go still. - Speaking of scheduling, the Niners will be off tomorrow then are expected to be in their first fully padded practice on Friday. Thus, this will be the last caveat about the lack of pads for this training camp as they were not in them again today. - Once again, coach Kyle Shanahan seems to be following the same routine each day. He came out just before 11 o'clock today during team drills and stayed through the end. It's still unclear how close he is to being back to full duty after his car crash but it appears to be trending the right direction. - New injuries to the list: WR Ricky Pearsall (right knee) did not practice and the Niners are concerned about it. They're "exploring all options" which presumably includes surgical options. A tough early blow for Pearsall, who is entering an important third season. S Malik Mustapha has a hamstring strain, which is also unfortunate given he's in an apparent competition with Marques Sigle for a starting safety job. - And, as feared Monday, RB Jordan James does have an injury. it's a rib fracture that will cost him some time. James had a really strong start to camp but his hold on the RB2 spot is far more tenuous as Kaelon Black gets more work (and seems to be doing really well with it). - Others not practicing because of injury: OT Vederian Lowe (high ankle sprain), DT Gracen Halton (knee bone bruise), WR Christian Kirk (calf). - Spotted working on the side Wednesday: Halton, RB Isaac Guerendo, DT Alfred Collins. Collins looks close to being ready and there's a chance he could be back in the mix as soon as Friday based on the timeline John Lynch provided on Saturday. - With Kirk and Pearsall out, the Niners tried out three receivers on Wednesday: Alex Bachman, D'Wayne Eskridge and Trenton Irwin. For those already on the roster, there's a whole lot of opportunity right now. Rookie De'Zhaun Stribling was already making a positive first impression and that continued on Wednesday. He's fast but has a smooth speed that seems to allow him to accelerate and decelerate with little issue. He's also big enough and unafraid to go over the middle. Had him down for five more catches Wednesday, including a nice job climbing the ladder on a high pass over the middle from Adrian Martinez. It's hard to say how things will shake out in terms of alignment but Stribling is working all three spots right now. My early guess: If Pearsall misses time, they'd like to go with Kirk or Demarcus Robinson at 'Z' and let Stribling handle the 'Y.' - Speaking of Robinson, it was a productive day for him Wednesday, also. Injuries to the position are a good reminder of why having someone like Robinson is helpful. A veteran who knows the offense and can step in anywhere is always useful. He connected with QB Brock Purdy multiple times, making a nice leaping catch over the middle on one. - Another solid day for Purdy, who took what the defense gave him and made some plays off schedule when the pass rush got some pressure. Had him at 14-of-18 in team drills. He was on point on in breakers to Jordan Watkins, Mike Evans and Stribling though he couldn't connect on a couple of deep balls. Watkins also had a good day with a handful of catches from multiple routes and situations. One he under threw a bit for Christian McCaffrey and LB Garret Wallow broke it up. Another, he threw well to Evans deep but it was a bit to the outside and CB Renardo Green (who is off to a strong start in this camp) got a hand on it and broke it up. - LB Dre Greenlaw is clearly energized by being back in San Francisco and has been around the ball a lot in the first few days. That started early Wednesday when he recovered (and possibly forced?) a fumble by Christian McCaffrey on one of the first plays of team drills. Couldn't quite tell who got a hand in there but Greenlaw was right there. - CB Jack Jones intercepted Mac Jones on a throw for Jacob Cowing. Jones has a reputation for making plays on the ball and also giving up some big ones but it's been more of the former than the latter through three open practices. - Black continues to impress as he gets more reps. James had an early edge but his rib injury really opens the door. I mentioned this before but Black's best quality might be how decisive he is and his burst to and through the line. OT Colton McKivitz said it's a bit unusual to see a rookie back put his foot in the ground and go like Black does but it's a positive sign for him that he's already got that skill. Pads will tell a better story but promising so far. - After a strong spring, it's been tougher sledding for Jacob Cowing in the first few days. He's had multiple passes thrown his way broken up or intercepted, sometimes because the defender has a size advantage. Today was better for Cowing but getting him the ball without having to scheme it up has been a challenge so far in this camp. - As a housekeeping measure: rookie EDGE Romello Height has switched numbers. He's wearing 58 now instead of 94. He was back at full speed after cramping issues Monday. - That's all for today. Niners are off tomorrow and back at it on Friday when the padded fun can begin. Thanks for reading, as always.
